claims.summary: For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2, with probability tending to one: for every y >= e^16, every j <= j*(y) = min(l_1, floor((log N)^(2/3)(log y)^(1/3))), and every Lipschitz G with int sum psi*_4(|d_i G|) <= 2 whose larger partial is at least y where grad G is nonzero, |sum_i G(X_i) - N int G| <= L' sqrt(N log N)(1 + Lambda_j(G)) with L' universal, Lambda_j the sum over cells of mesh 2^(-j) of Lip(G on Q) area(Q). The same holds with the cellwise sum over any balanced dyadic partition with cells of level at most j*(y). The witness of lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound at (4,4), built with the reduction's parameter L >= 132, has Lambda_(l_1) <= 297/L, so the bound is of the conjectured order on it, against Lebesgue measure.
claims.assessment: Working proof: lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split with the gradient mass bounded by 8 (log y)^(-1/4) through psi*_4(t) >= t (log t)^(1/4)/2 on the larger partial; the witness's Lambda computed column by column over the Leighton-Shor graph, with the breakpoint columns negligible.
claims.rationale: Replaces the thickness condition of the single-level case by a bounded cellwise Lipschitz sum and shows the class lower bound's thin witness meets it (an elementary layer-cake bound also gives that witness's order); the open single-level case is functions whose cellwise sum is large at every allowed mesh.
claims.next_action: The fourth route review; then whether many parallel thin bands of one small gradient level, with alternating slopes, have discrepancy beyond sqrt(N log N).
